allocation_gate_rows.evidence: CBO lists materially different implementation examples but selects no force size, unit mix, mission, or posture path.
No allocation protects training, maintenance, materiel availability, personnel safety, or operational-risk controls.
The option mentions a possible 17 percent active-component reduction by 2034 but does not select or cost active, reserve, civilian, contractor, family, or community effects.
The 2026 request shifts substantial acquisition funding through reconciliation, while the option supplies no program, quantity, milestone, cancellation, or delivery schedule.
No threshold or stress path covers munitions depth, sealift and airlift, surge, supplier capacity, or industrial-base continuity.
Greater allied provision is only an example; no treaty, region, timing, allied-capacity, or burden-transfer case is selected.
No implementation, severance, base-closure, contract termination, schedule-slip, or adverse-realization cost is quantified.
The December 2024 DoD option is not reconciled to the February 2026 all-national-defense baseline or the enacted mandatory-defense funding path.

risk_findings: GAO's July 2026 assessment reports delayed milestones and immature technologies among major acquisition programs, so assumed procurement efficiencies cannot be credited without program evidence.
GAO's April 2026 sustainment review reports critical operating-and-support cost growth in 14 of 36 reviewed systems, so readiness-preserving sustainment reductions require system-level plans.
CBO reports uncertainty over whether reconciliation-funded acquisition is one-time or substitutes for enduring base-budget requirements, preventing a clean baseline allocation.

candidate_decision.next_candidate_strategy: select a mission and force-structure case, allocate annual reductions by appropriation and program, preserve readiness floors, and cost transition and execution risk before rescoring

public_warning: The $959 billion option is rejected for package admission because it does not choose or cost a force, readiness, personnel, procurement, allied-burden, or transition allocation. Eight required gates remain blocked; this is not evidence that every possible defense reduction would fail.
